title: Gen-4.5 Tops MidcenturyAI Physics Bench with 30% Score
summary:
Most leading video world models fail to maintain physical accuracy within a few frames of generation. MidcenturyAI's new MC-PhysBench assessment, which tested more than 6,000 videos across 15 models and 9 scenes, ranked Gen-4.5 as the top performer with a score of 30% and Cosmos 3 Super in second with 21%.

The benchmark measures "Time To Failure" by providing models with a single frame from a 1 second simulated physics clip and a text description, then requiring them to generate the following 2 seconds. Failure occurs when a physical violation—such as objects vanishing or passing through each other—persists for at least 0.3 seconds. Results are averaged over 50 identical episodes per scene to ensure a distribution of failures rather than single lucky outputs.

selectedTweets.text:
Today, @MidcenturyAI is introducing MC-PhysBench: A Time-to-Failure Physics Benchmark for World Models.

The benchmark gives a world model one still frame from the end of a 1s simulated physics clip + a short text desc.

The WM must generate the next 2 seconds. MC-PhysBench then asks: how long does that continuation remain inside the range of futures that physics permits?

The score is Time To Failure: the first moment a physical violation persists for at least 0.3 seconds. 

The bench also produces survival curves and categorizes the specific failure type, such as:

> an object vanishing
> moving incorrectly
> passing through another object
> or the camera drifting.

Each result is averaged over 50 identical episodes per scene, so it reflects a distribution of failures rather than one lucky/unlucky generation.

Gen-4.5 ranks #1 the benchmark with a 30% score, Cosmos 3 Super ranks #2 with 21%.

Superb work done by @shilpishahh and @B_S_N_Y 👏
